html:
RDS-1 was the first Soviet atomic bomb, set off on 29 August 1949 at the Semipalatinsk test site on the Kazakh steppe. Its yield was about 22 kilotons, similar to the bomb dropped on Nagasaki.

The project was led by the physicist Igor Kurchatov and overseen by the secret police chief Lavrentiy Beria. It moved fast after the atomic bombings of Japan in 1945. Spies inside the American programme, above all Klaus Fuchs, passed on details, and RDS-1 was closely based on the American Fat Man design.

American planes detected radioactive traces in the air within days, and President Truman announced the test in September. The United States had lost its monopoly years sooner than expected. The Cold War arms race began in earnest, and Semipalatinsk became the site of hundreds more tests, with lasting harm to the people nearby (see Semipalatinsk fallout).
